metadata.subject: Operating Systems
metadata.title: Translate Virtual Addresses
metadata.description: Calculate address translations and recognize nonresident pages.

learning_objectives: Split an address into page and offset.
Read a page table and presence bit.
Distinguish page faults from invalid addresses.

mission.title: Translate an address yourself
mission.description: Calculate each part and follow the mapping to physical memory.

introduction.title: A program's address is not a RAM location
introduction.content: Programs use logical addresses. Paging divides them into fixed-size pages. A page table tells us which physical RAM frame holds each page.
points: The page number identifies a page; the offset identifies a byte inside it.
A frame holds a whole page of the same size.
Later, NOT PRESENT will mean the allocated page is not in RAM: a page fault.

worked_example.title: One translation, worked through
worked_example.content: Page size 100 bytes; address 207. Page 2 maps to frame 4.

steps.explanation: Two complete 100-byte pages fit before 207; 7 bytes remain.
The page table maps logical page 2 to physical frame 4.
Frame 4 begins at byte 400. Move 7 bytes into it.

worked_example.conclusion: The location changes, but the byte keeps its offset.

next.title: Now calculate a new address.
next.content: Answers stay hidden until you submit each calculation.

action_explanations.page: The page identifies the fixed-size region containing the address.
action_explanations.offset: The offset is the byte position within that page.
action_explanations.frame: The matching table entry determines residency and the frame.
action_explanations.physicalAddress: Combine the mapped frame and unchanged offset; see the calculation evidence beside your result.

visualization.order_message: Complete the current calculation before moving to the next field.

page.title: Calculate the page number
page.instruction: How many complete {pageSize}-byte pages fit before address {logicalAddress}?
page.retry: Try again. Determine how many complete {pageSize}-byte pages fit before address {logicalAddress}; discard the fractional part.

offset.title: Calculate the offset
offset.instruction: How many bytes remain after those complete pages?
offset.retry: Subtract the bytes in all complete pages from the logical address. The remainder must be smaller than the page size.
offset.accepted: Offset {answer} is the position inside the page.

frame.title: Find the frame or page fault
frame.instruction: Use your page number to find its row. Enter the frame, or PAGE_FAULT if NOT PRESENT.
frame.retry: Use the row for your logical page, not the offset. NOT PRESENT means PAGE_FAULT; otherwise read its frame.
frame.accepted: Lookup result: {answer}. The presence bit tells you whether RAM holds the page.

physicalAddress.title: Calculate the physical address
physicalAddress.instruction: Combine the frame and unchanged offset. If the page is not resident, enter PAGE_FAULT.
physicalAddress.retry: Start at frame × page size, then add the offset. A nonresident page has no physical address: enter PAGE_FAULT.

quiz.question: What does a page table provide?

discovery.title: Paging discovery
discovery.summary: Address translation turns a logical page number into a physical frame while preserving its offset.

sections.title: What? Logical pages and physical frames
sections.content: Logical addresses are divided into fixed-size pages, mapped to equally sized frames in RAM.

sections.title: Example: split, look up, combine
sections.content: With size 100, address 207 is page 2, offset 7. If page 2 maps to frame 4, the physical address is 407.

sections.title: Why preserve the offset?
sections.content: A whole page moves to a frame. Its bytes keep their positions inside the block.

sections.title: Page fault versus invalid address
sections.content: NOT PRESENT means an allocated page is not in RAM: a page fault. An address outside the configured range, or with no allocated mapping here, is invalid. This lesson does not simulate loading or replacement.

sections.title: Remember
sections.content: Page = complete pages. Offset = remainder. Frame = table lookup. Physical = frame × page size + offset.

alternate_explanations.title: Numbered storage boxes
alternate_explanations.content: The table says which storage box holds a page. A byte keeps its place inside the box even when the box has a different number.

alternate_explanations.title: Try a smaller address
alternate_explanations.content: With size 10, address 23 is page 2, offset 3. If page 2 lives in frame 6, find byte 63.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, why does the offset stay the same during paging translation?
recall.model_answer: The page table changes the page's location to a frame. Since pages and frames have the same size, a byte keeps its offset.
